elements.element: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates)
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates"

elements.element: Covers third-party claims alleging Services/Deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "(a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Covers data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "(c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor"

elements.element: Covers Vendor gross negligence / wilful misconduct

"allow the indemnifying party to control the defence with counsel of its choice"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content

"procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them ... Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap appears; 21.3 merely lists "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims with no 3× annual fees cap.

offending_extra_words: and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)
Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor
The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its own cost.
The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party without its prior written consent.
reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are present in operative text: Vendor defence/indemnity for Customer and Affiliates across IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; notice/control/cooperation procedure; and a Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. The locked preferred level is satisfied.

The fallback bargain is not independently satisfied because no 3× annual fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity obligations is inserted anywhere; this is irrelevant to the locked target but must not be mixed with the preferred package.

Minimality fails: the insertion adds hold-harmless language, an express damages/attorneys'-fees enumeration, Vendor Technology as an indemnified subject, a Customer defence duty, an indemnitee participation right, and settlement-consent mechanics — none of which appear in the preferred prose (notice, control, cooperation only).

Intent is preserved: Section 9.3's cross-reference to Section 20.5 now resolves to the infringement-remedies paragraph, no defined term is left dangling, and Sections 19.5 and 21.3 remain effective. The heading anchoring should nonetheless be placed after the preceding section's final body paragraph rather than after an existing heading.
